$comment: The specs' own JSON examples, classified. See README.md. Every fenced json/jsonc document in docs/specs/*.md must appear here exactly once, or packages/core/test/spec-examples.test.ts fails. Keys are `file#fence.position` — the fence's ordinal in the file, NOT its line number. Line numbers were the key twice and broke twice, because editing a spec above a block is a normal thing to do and remapping a manifest afterwards teaches nobody anything. An ordinal still moves when a block is added, removed or reordered, which is the change worth a second look.

examples.note: The spec elides REFERENCE_FLEET with a comment; the fixture echoes the published constant, which is what the endpoint does.
The spec writes NE and says "… N, S, SE". The other three are filled in, because the route answers with four and the schema says so.

The spec's block writes NE alone with no elision marker, so it reads as complete and is not. The route answers with four subsystems, which is what makes national.derived = sum_of_four true; the fixture is the four.

The spec writes published_at as the bare string "…", which reads as data rather than as an elision. It is an instant, and gate_at(target_date, gate_profile) is the whole argument for the boundary decision, so the fixture states one.

The spec elides the ForecastOrigin ("the same object as the forecast route's") and the peak-hour eight, but writes `drivers` as a one-element list with no elision marker even though its own prose two paragraphs later says all eight groups are returned, ranked by |share|; the fixture is the eight. `driver_group_hash` is written "sha256:…", which is prose. vintage_fidelity is added rather than changed: the block never states it and vocabulary rule 9 requires it.
The spec writes one group and says "... eight entries, ranked by |share|".
One fence, two documents: the battery variant.

The shiftable-load variant. Its 70 MW against 1200 MWh/day is the SHIFT_EXCEEDS_BASELINE case the spec names in its own prose - a cross-field rule the gateway validates and a schema cannot express, which is why this validates here and would be a 422 at the boundary.
The spec elides the assets; the fixture uses REFERENCE_FLEET, which is the one fleet every published figure is measured against.
The spec writes scenario_hash as "sha256:…", which reads as a stated value. A hash is 64 hex characters and the schema says so, because a hash that is not one is a cache key that never matches.
Same as the optimization result. Everything else the spec elides - the 24 hours on both sides, the dispatch, the executed plan, the episodes and the solver receipt - is filled in.
